Wait - the user says they can't find Mount Everest. Everest is at lat 27.99, lng 86.93. With the initial region centered at lat 30, lng 10 and delta 120, that should show from -50 to 110 longitude and -30 to 90 latitude. Everest at lng 86.93 should be visible.
 
The problem could be that react-native-maps is struggling to render all 100 markers at once, or the map isn't initializing properly on their device. But if they're on web, they'd be seeing the fallback view instead - though they mentioned seeing some mountains, which suggests the map is actually rendering. Let me look at the mountain coordinates themselves to see if there's bad data causing rendering issues.

Actually, wait - if they can't find Mount Everest specifically, that's a big clue. The web fallback only displays summited mountains, so if they're on web, they wouldn't see Everest unless it's marked as summited. I should update the fallback to show all mountains instead of just the summited ones. And since react-native-maps is polyfilled on web according to the system info, I can remove the web check entirely and let the actual map component work across all platforms.

The issue is that the map screen has a `Platform.OS === 'web'` check that forces a fallback view on web, and that fallback only shows **summited** mountains. Also, `react-native-maps` is polyfilled for web, so we don't need that web check. Let me fix this.

The fix is applied. The map was skipping the actual map view on web and only showing the fallback (which listed only summited mountains). Now it will render the interactive map with all 100 mountain markers on web too, since `react-native-maps` is supported there. You should now be able to see all mountains including Everest.
